correctness.rationale: The pinned package defines PS as continuous unit-rate eating, RP as average over uniform agent permutations, and each received r-th choice earns n-r Borda points. Object relabeling is free because the first agent has a strict order, reducing all (n!)^n profiles to (n!)^(n-1) canonical profiles with n! multiplicity. An independently written rational PS event simulator and RP recursive Bellman welfare evaluator enumerated all canonical profiles n=2,3,4; n=4 has exactly 13824 reps, giving over all 331776 labelled profiles 87408 positive, 129168 zero and 115200 negative PS-minus-RP values; mean 1283/62208>0. n=3: 36 negatives at -1/12 and mean -1/72; n=2 all zero. The source also cross-checks matrix and direct-welfare implementations. For every n>4, new agents each rank their fresh personal object first and all old agents rank old objects above new ones: both rules preserve old four-agent lotteries and only shift each old Borda score by constant n-4, so the positive and negative four-agent witness signs persist.
residual_risks: Exact n<=4 values rely on complete rational enumeration modulo an explicitly free object-relabeling group, not a probabilistic sample.
Only sign existence, not full profile enumeration, is proved for all n>=4; impartial culture and equally spaced Borda utilities are essential.

value.rationale: At the smallest postclassical market size, this natural rank-welfare comparison exhibits a sharp mean sign change even though more individual profiles favor the opposite mechanism. The exhaustive exact distribution is an interpretable quantitative decision-theory invariant and the sign-persistence construction shows its robust logical scope.
residual_risks: Model interpretation depends on impartial culture and equally spaced Borda scores; it says nothing about actual cardinal welfare or incentive behavior.
